steps.description:
Smart home systems are becoming increasingly popular in modern homes, making it convenient to control devices via a mobile app. In this challenge, you'll be simulating a remote control.

As you begin adding logic to your code, your program can respond to different inputs or conditions. This is known as branching. Pay close attention to how each question guides you to break the problem into parts. Once you know how to break things down, finding the solution becomes much easier.


You'll be coding a Remote Control app for your home air conditioning, with a toggle for ON/OFF. It beeps once when turned ON and twice when OFF.


By observing the clip, you can briefly breakdown the program sequence into two parts: 

  • PART 1: Turning it from OFF to ON.
  • PART 2: Turning it from ON to OFF.

Let's do the FIRST PART:

1. Display "Aircon OFF" on the LCD wait until Button D24 is pressed and released.

2. Upon release, make a short beep.

3. Display "Aircon ON"

Use Repeat Until, Repeat While or Wait Until blocks in your code.

You are coding a Remote Control app for your home air conditioning, with a toggle for ON/OFF. It beeps once when turned ON and twice when OFF.

By observing the clip, you can briefly breakdown the program sequence into two parts: 

  • PART 1: Turning it from OFF to ON.
  • PART 2: Turning it from ON to OFF.

1. Display "Aircon OFF" on the LCD wait until Button D24 is pressed and released.

2. Upon release, make a short beep.

3. Display "Aircon ON" on the LCD wait until Button D24 is pressed and released.

4. Upon release, make two short beeps.

5. The program repeats from Step (1).

Use Repeat Until, Repeat While or Wait Until blocks in your code.
